assignments.title: 22.7 Primary Source Report: The Wannsee Protocol and What Was Known
assignments.html:
PRIMARY SOURCE REPORT
The Wannsee Protocol and What Was Known
A record of 1942 read alongside what the Allies learned.
Report · 16 points · Word document upload
☼ ─ ☼ ─ ☼
HOW TO WORK
Read the two lessons and the two primary sources first, and look over your notes in My Notebook. Then write your report in Word and submit it as the submission box below describes.
THE TASK

Write a report of 450 to 650 words in Word. Answer all four questions below, in order, each under its own heading. Use the Wannsee Protocol excerpt and “The Holocaust: Wannsee and What the Allies Knew”. Put short quotations in quotation marks and cite each one in a footnote.

This subject deserves plain, careful, respectful writing. State the facts as the sources give them, and do not add details you have not read. You will be graded on the quality of your argument, not on which side you take.

YOUR REPORT

1. Read the Wannsee Protocol excerpt. In your own words, what does it say is to happen to the Jews of Europe? Then name what the passage never says in plain words, and explain what phrases such as “fall away by natural diminution” and “treated accordingly” stand for.

2. “The Holocaust: Wannsee and What the Allies Knew” says the conference “was not the moment the killing was decided” but the moment when the officials of a modern state agreed to organize it. Use the passage to show how the document supports that claim. Why would officials write in this way, and what does the lesson mean when it says the clerks were as necessary as the guards?

3. “The Holocaust: Wannsee and What the Allies Knew” says the Allies “knew a great deal”. Name two pieces of information that reached them, with the dates. Then compare the kind of evidence the Protocol gives a historian with the kind of reports the Allies received in 1942 and 1944. What can each show, and what can each not show?

4. In the summer of 1944 Jewish leaders asked the Allies to bomb Auschwitz or the railways that led to it. Suppose the Allies had agreed. Using the lesson’s arguments on both sides, say what might have followed, and what you think would have been gained or lost. Then say what you cannot know.

GRADING RUBRIC (16 pts)

SUBMISSION

Write your report in Word and save it to your OneDrive folder. Then open this assignment in Canvas, choose the OneDrive tab, select your file, and submit.

Your teacher will read your report and score it with the rubric above.

quizzes.description:
MODULE INTRODUCTION
Module Introduction: The Tide Turns, and the Reckoning
Survey · 3 questions · not graded
☼ ─ ☼ ─ ☼
Before you start

Welcome to The Tide Turns, and the Reckoning. Answer the questions below before you open the first lesson. Your answers help your teacher see where the class is starting. This survey is not graded.

This module's goals:
  • Explain how the battles of Stalingrad and El Alamein, D-Day, and the Bulge turned the war.
  • Describe how Nazi persecution of the Jews grew into mass murder and what the Wannsee Conference was and was not.
  • Weigh what the Allies knew, when they knew it, and what choices they had.

discussions.title: 22.8 Discussion: What did the Allies know, and what could they have done?
discussions.html:
DISCUSSION
What did the Allies know, and what could they have done?
Three questions to keep apart: what was known, what was possible, what was decided.
Graded discussion · 10 points · one post and one reply
☼ ─ ☼ ─ ☼
HOW TO WORK
Read the two lessons and the two primary sources first, and look over your notes in My Notebook. Then post your answer to the prompt below, and reply to one classmate.
DISCUSSION PROMPT

This week’s question: What did the Allies know, and what could they have done?

Keep three things apart in your answer: what the Allied governments knew and when, what choices they had and what each would have cost, and what they decided. Choose one choice, such as admitting refugees, bombing the railways, or rescue through victory, and say whether you think it was the right one. Use the evidence in “The Holocaust: Wannsee and What the Allies Knew”.

Write 150 to 250 words. State one claim you believe is true. Then explain why, using the specific evidence named above. Write plainly and with respect. Keep to what the lessons and the sources show. If you are guessing, say so.

RESPOND TO A CLASSMATE

Reply to one classmate. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with a fact or decision they did not use. If not, say politely where you think it falls short, and give your reason.

GRADING RUBRIC (10 pts)
CriteriaSubstantive (full credit)Thin (partial credit)Missing (no credit)
